candidate_relations.reason: Complex orbital cyst is a broad, non-specific category that encompasses dermoid cysts but does not commit to the dermoid subtype required by the reference diagnosis.
Orbital dermoid is a standard alias for orbital dermoid cyst, fully capturing the dermoid subtype and orbital location consistent with the clinical and imaging findings.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Orbital dermoid = dermoid cyst of the orbit; harmless wording variant

candidate_relations.reason: Epidermoid cysts are related ectodermal inclusion cysts but differ from dermoid cysts by the absence of dermal appendages (hair follicles, sebaceous glands). The imaging characteristics (T2 hyperintense, FLAIR hypointense, no diffusion restriction) and superolateral location at the frontozygomatic suture are more characteristic of dermoid than epidermoid, making this an incompatible subtype.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Epidermoid cyst is a distinct subtype lacking dermal adnexal elements

candidate_relations.reason: Orbital Dermoid Cyst directly and completely names the reference diagnosis with all required components (dermoid subtype, cystic nature, orbital location), consistent with all clinical and imaging features described.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Orbital Dermoid Cyst is the full explicit label matching the reference

candidate_relations.reason: Orbital lymphangioma is a distinct vascular lesion that can present as a cystic orbital mass in children but is a different diagnostic entity. The well-circumscribed extraconal location at the frontozygomatic suture, smooth bone remodeling, FLAIR hypointensity, and absence of internal enhancement argue against lymphangioma and favor dermoid cyst.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Orbital lymphangioma is a vascular malformation, not a dermoid cyst

case_quality_flags: Classic presentation of superolateral orbital dermoid cyst with characteristic imaging features; reference diagnosis well-supported by clinical record
